title: UGC NET Psychology — Study Hub
subtitle: Focused Psychology preparation: clear concepts, active recall and spaced revision.

units.title: Emergence of Psychology
units.description: Build the story of psychology as a discipline: where its questions came from, how Indian and Western intellectual traditions shaped them, and how major schools and paradigms changed the subject. Move from philosophical roots to the emergence of scientific psychology, then compare the assumptions, methods, and objects of study that distinguish major traditions. By the end of the unit, you should be able to place major thinkers and schools in context and explain why psychology developed in different directions.

parts.title: Western Psychology and Foundations
parts.description: Trace the emergence of Western psychology, major schools, founding paths, knowledge foundations, paradigms and paradigmatic controversies.

parts.title: Indian Psychology
parts.description: Study Indian psychological thought, traditions and their distinctive approaches to self, mind, knowledge and transformation.

topics.title: Eastern Psychological Thought
topics.explanation: Understand each tradition as a source of psychological ideas. Compare its view of self, mind, suffering, knowledge, discipline and transformation. Keep the traditions distinct rather than treating them as interchangeable.

microtopics.title: Bhagavad Gita: Karma Yoga and Equanimity

topics.title: Development of Academic Psychology in India
topics.explanation: Build a chronology.

topics.title: Colonialism, Postcolonialism and Disciplinary Identity
topics.explanation: Study these as questions about the development and identity of psychology in India: influence of colonial knowledge systems, postcolonial critique, and the search for a distinct disciplinary identity.

topics.title: Western Psychology: Greek, Medieval and Modern Thought
topics.explanation: Organize Western intellectual history into Greek, medieval and modern periods. Focus on how ideas about mind, knowledge and human nature changed across these periods.

topics.title: Major Schools and Movements of Western Psychology
topics.explanation: Create a timeline of major schools and movements. For each, learn its central question, subject matter, method/approach and distinctive contribution.

topics.title: Four Founding Paths of Academic Psychology
topics.explanation: Prepare a four-person comparison.

topics.title: Crisis of the Experimental-Analytical Paradigm
topics.explanation: Study the criticism that an exclusively experimental-analytical orientation can narrow the range of psychological questions and methods. Connect this with the later emergence of alternative paradigms.

topics.title: Indic Influences on Modern Psychology
topics.explanation: Identify ways Indic traditions have contributed concepts, practices or questions relevant to modern psychological thought. Keep this separate from the broader history of Indian psychology.

topics.title: Knowledge Foundations: Ontology, Epistemology and Methodology
topics.explanation: Ontology asks what is assumed to exist; epistemology asks how knowledge is possible or justified; methodology concerns how inquiry is conducted. Learn the distinction and their relationship within a paradigm.

topics.title: Paradigms of Western Psychology
topics.explanation: Make a paradigm comparison chart. For each paradigm, learn its assumptions about reality/knowledge and its preferred approach to inquiry. The syllabus expects these six named paradigms.

topics.title: Paradigmatic Controversies
topics.explanation: Study controversies between different assumptions about psychological knowledge, methods, objectivity, subjectivity and the status of scientific explanation.

topics.title: Indian Paradigms of Psychological Knowledge
topics.explanation: Compare the five named Indian paradigms in terms of knowledge, self, mind and transformation. Do not collapse them into one generic 'Indian psychology'.

topics.title: Science and Spirituality
topics.explanation: Study the relationship between scientific and spiritual ways of knowing in the syllabus context, including the distinction between avidya and vidya.

topics.title: Self-Knowledge in Indian Psychology
topics.explanation: Focus on self-knowledge as a central theme in Indian psychology and relate it to the traditions named earlier in the unit.

units.title: Research Methodology and Statistics
units.description: Build a complete research-to-evidence framework for psychology. Start with how research questions become variables, hypotheses, samples, designs, and ethical decisions, then connect these choices to measurement, data collection, and interpretation. In the statistics portion, develop the reasoning behind probability, distributions, statistical tests, power, effect size, correlation, regression, and factor analysis so that you can identify which method fits a research question and interpret what the result actually means.

parts.title: Research Methodology
parts.description: Build the research process from research problems and variables through hypotheses, sampling, designs, methods, ethics and research paradigms.

parts.title: Statistics and Data Analysis
parts.description: Develop the statistical toolkit used in psychological research, including descriptive statistics, probability, testing, ANOVA, correlation, regression and multivariate methods.

topics.title: Research: Meaning, Purpose and Dimensions
topics.explanation: Define research as systematic inquiry and organize its purposes and dimensions before studying specific designs and methods.

topics.title: Research Problems, Variables, Hypotheses and Sampling
topics.explanation: Build the research sequence: problem → variables → operational definitions → hypothesis → sampling. Be able to distinguish conceptual variables from their operational definitions.

microtopics.title: Type I and Type II errors

topics.title: Research Ethics
topics.explanation: Study ethical conduct during participation, data collection, analysis, authorship and reporting. Focus on integrity, participant protection and responsible reporting.

topics.title: Research Paradigms
topics.explanation: Compare quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods approaches by their aims, kinds of data, logic of inquiry and integration of evidence.

topics.title: Methods of Research
topics.explanation: Create a method matrix. For every named method, learn purpose, data source, typical procedure, strengths and limitations.

topics.title: Statistics in Psychology
topics.explanation: Central tendency summarizes the typical location of scores; dispersion describes spread. Master mean, median, mode, range, variance and standard deviation.

topics.title: Normal Probability Curve
topics.explanation: Study the shape and properties of the normal distribution and its relationship with standard deviation and standardized scores.

topics.title: Parametric and Non-Parametric Tests
topics.explanation: Make a decision table for the listed tests: independent/dependent structure, number of groups, measurement assumptions and whether the test is parametric or non-parametric.

topics.title: Power Analysis
topics.explanation: Study statistical power as the probability of detecting an effect when an effect of the specified kind exists. Connect power with sample size, effect size and significance criteria.

topics.title: Effect Size
topics.explanation: Study effect size as an index of the magnitude of an effect, complementing significance testing.

topics.title: Correlational Analysis
topics.explanation: Distinguish Pearson/Product Moment and Rank Order approaches, then learn how partial and multiple correlation extend correlation analysis.

topics.title: Special Correlation Methods
topics.explanation: Learn which variable formats each special coefficient is designed for. Make a variable-type → coefficient table.

topics.title: Regression
topics.explanation: Study prediction using one predictor versus multiple predictors, including the meaning of regression coefficients and prediction.

topics.title: Factor Analysis
topics.explanation: Organize factor analysis into assumptions → extraction/method → rotation → interpretation. Learn how observed variables are represented through underlying factors.

topics.title: Experimental Designs
topics.explanation: Create a design-selection map. Match each design with number/type of variables, groups, repeated observations, control structure and purpose.

topics.title: ANOVA
topics.explanation: Study analysis of variance separately from the broader experimental-design family. Focus on the logic of variance partitioning, one-way and factorial ANOVA, interactions and interpretation.

units.title: Psychological Testing
units.description: Understand psychological testing as a systematic process rather than a collection of test names. Follow the path from test construction and standardisation through reliability, validity, norms, administration, scoring, and interpretation. Then connect these foundations with major types and applications of psychological assessment so you can distinguish what a test measures, how confidently it measures it, and how its results should be interpreted.

topics.title: Types of Tests
topics.explanation: Classify psychological tests by purpose, format and area of assessment. Build a master taxonomy before learning individual instruments.

topics.title: Test Construction
topics.explanation: Study the sequence from defining the construct and writing items to item analysis and selection of effective items.

topics.title: Test Standardisation: Reliability, Validity and Norms
topics.explanation: Organize standardization around consistent administration/scoring, reliability, validity and norms. Distinguish reliability from validity.

topics.title: Areas of Psychological Testing
topics.explanation: Create an assessment-domain map: what each test area attempts to measure and where it is applied.

topics.title: Attitude Scales and Computer-Based Testing
topics.explanation: Compare the three named attitude scaling formats, then study how psychological testing can be delivered through computers.

topics.title: Applications of Psychological Testing: Clinical, Organizational, Educational, Counseling, Military and Career Guidance
topics.explanation: Map assessment applications to setting, purpose and decisions supported by test information.

units.title: Biological Basis of Behavior
units.description: Connect behaviour with the biological systems that make it possible. Study the organisation and functioning of the nervous system, brain structures and processes, sensory systems, endocrine influences, and genetic contributions, then use these foundations to explain links with cognition, emotion, motivation, and behaviour. The unit is designed to help you move between biological mechanisms and psychological outcomes rather than memorising structures in isolation.

topics.title: Sensory Systems
topics.explanation: Study sensory systems through stimulus → receptor → neural processing. Distinguish general and specific sensations.

topics.title: Neurons and Neural Transmission
topics.explanation: Learn neuron structure and function, types of neurons, generation/propagation of neural impulses and synaptic transmission.

topics.title: Neurotransmitters
topics.explanation: Study neurotransmitters as chemical messengers involved in neural communication and relate major systems to behaviour where relevant.

topics.title: Central and Peripheral Nervous Systems
topics.explanation: Compare CNS and PNS structurally and functionally, including their major divisions.

microtopics.title: Spinal cord and autonomic nervous system

topics.title: Neuroplasticity
topics.explanation: Study the capacity of the nervous system to change structurally or functionally in relation to experience, learning, development or injury.

topics.title: Methods of Physiological Psychology
topics.explanation: Create an invasive versus non-invasive comparison. For each named method learn what is measured/manipulated and what kind of inference it permits.

topics.title: Muscular and Glandular Systems
topics.explanation: Study muscular and glandular systems, then connect biological mechanisms with hunger, thirst, sleep and sexual motivation.

topics.title: Biological Basis of Emotion
topics.explanation: Study limbic-system involvement and hormonal regulation as biological bases of emotional behaviour.

topics.title: Genetics and Behaviour
topics.explanation: Study genetic and environmental contributions to behaviour and understand why twin and adoption studies are used in the nature-nurture question.

units.title: Attention, Perception, Learning, Memory and Forgetting
units.description: Follow the flow of information from attention and perception through learning, memory, and forgetting. First understand how people select, organise, and interpret incoming information, including perceptual organisation, constancy, illusions, and signal detection. Then connect this with how behaviour and knowledge change through learning, how information is encoded and stored in memory, and why remembering and forgetting take the forms they do across major theories and models.

parts.title: Attention and Perception
parts.description: Build the foundations of attention and perception, from selective processing and signal detection to perceptual organization and higher-order perception.

parts.title: Learning, Memory and Forgetting
parts.description: Move from major learning theories and conditioning to memory systems, retrieval, forgetting and applied behaviour change.

topics.title: Attention
topics.explanation: Distinguish forms of attention and compare models according to how they explain selection and processing of information.

topics.title: Perception
topics.explanation: Use this as the umbrella topic for the perception subtopics that follow: organization, constancy, depth, movement and contextual influences.

topics.title: Approaches to Perception
topics.explanation: Compare Gestalt explanations with physiological approaches to perception.

topics.title: Perceptual Organisation
topics.explanation: Study how perceptual systems organize input, including figure-ground separation and Gestalt laws of organization.

topics.title: Perceptual Constancy and Illusions
topics.explanation: Study constancies, illusions and the perception of form, depth and movement as distinct but related perceptual problems.

topics.title: Motivation and Learning in Perception
topics.explanation: Study how prior learning and motivational factors can influence perceptual interpretation.

topics.title: Signal Detection Theory
topics.explanation: Study detection as a decision process influenced by signal strength, noise and response criteria, and learn its applications.

topics.title: Advanced Topics in Perception
topics.explanation: Make a multi-part revision map covering subliminal perception, information processing, cultural influences, perceptual styles, pattern recognition and ecological approaches.

topics.title: Learning Process
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Learning Process, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

topics.title: Classical Conditioning
topics.explanation: Study the conditioning procedure, terminology, major phenomena and theoretical issues associated with classical conditioning.

topics.title: Instrumental Learning
topics.explanation: Study learning through consequences and compare major instrumental-learning paradigms and phenomena.

topics.title: Reinforcement
topics.explanation: Study reinforcement variables and schedules and learn how schedule differences affect responding.

topics.title: Behaviour Modification
topics.explanation: Connect learning principles with systematic behaviour modification and its applications.

topics.title: Cognitive Approaches to Learning
topics.explanation: Study learning that involves cognitive representations and observational processes, including latent and observational learning.

topics.title: Verbal and Discrimination Learning
topics.explanation: Study learning involving verbal material and the acquisition of discriminations between stimuli or response categories.

topics.title: Recent Trends in Learning
topics.explanation: Connect learning with neurophysiological mechanisms and contemporary biological approaches to learning.

topics.title: Memory Processes
topics.explanation: Organize memory around encoding, storage and retrieval and understand their distinct roles.

topics.title: Stages of Memory
topics.explanation: Compare the major memory stages/systems and distinguish episodic, semantic and procedural memory.

topics.title: Theories of Forgetting
topics.explanation: Compare the four named explanations for forgetting and identify the mechanism emphasized by each.

units.title: Thinking, Intelligence and Creativity
units.description: Understand thinking as a set of related processes involved in representing information, using concepts and language, solving problems, and making decisions. Then connect these processes with major approaches to intelligence and the study of creativity. The unit emphasises distinctions among theories while also showing how thinking, intelligence, and creativity can be applied to everyday situations and exam-style problems.

parts.title: Thinking
parts.description: Study the cognitive processes used to represent problems, reason, solve problems and make decisions.

parts.title: Intelligence and Creativity
parts.description: Compare major approaches to intelligence and creativity, including their models, assessment and applications.

topics.title: Perspectives on Thought Processes
topics.explanation: Compare the four perspectives by asking how each explains thought, organization and processing of information.

topics.title: Concept Formation and Reasoning
topics.explanation: Study how concepts are formed, the roles of rules/types/strategies, and the major forms of reasoning.

topics.title: Language and Thought
topics.explanation: Study the relationship between language and thought and organize competing positions clearly.

topics.title: Problem Solving and Decision Making
topics.explanation: Separate problem solving from decision making, then compare types, strategies, obstacles and models.

topics.title: Metacognition
topics.explanation: Distinguish knowing about one's cognition from regulating and monitoring one's cognitive processes.

topics.title: Theories of Intelligence
topics.explanation: Build a theorist-by-model table. The syllabus expects familiarity with each named contributor/framework.

topics.title: Theories of Creativity
topics.explanation: Build a parallel theorist map for the named creativity approaches and measures.

topics.title: Relationship Between Intelligence and Creativity
topics.explanation: Study the major ways intelligence and creativity may be related and avoid reducing one construct to the other.

units.title: Personality, Motivation, Emotion, Stress and Coping
units.description: Examine the person as an organised system of personality, motives, emotions, and responses to demands. Compare major approaches to personality and then connect motivation and emotion with goals, self-regulation, achievement, curiosity, sensation seeking, and flow. Finally, understand stress and coping as processes shaped by appraisal, resources, and responses, so you can integrate the unit instead of studying each topic as a separate list of theories.

parts.title: Personality
parts.description: Compare major approaches to personality, including trait, psychoanalytic, social-cognitive, humanistic and related perspectives.

parts.title: Motivation, Emotion, Stress and Coping
parts.description: Connect motivational processes with emotion, stress, coping and psychological adaptation.

topics.title: Determinants of Personality
topics.explanation: Compare biological and sociocultural influences on personality and consider their interaction.

topics.title: Approaches to Personality
topics.explanation: Build a master comparison of the eight named approaches using assumptions, core concepts and view of personality.

topics.title: Rotter's Locus of Control
topics.explanation: Study these as three distinct frameworks: locus of control, explanatory style and moral development.

topics.title: Basic Motivational Concepts
topics.explanation: Create a concept chain and distinguish the six motivational terms.

topics.title: Approaches to Motivation
topics.explanation: Compare the four named approaches by their proposed sources and mechanisms of motivation.

topics.title: Exploratory Behaviour and Curiosity
topics.explanation: Study exploration and curiosity as motivational processes associated with seeking information or stimulation.

topics.title: Sensation Seeking
topics.explanation: Learn sensation seeking as a personality-motivation construct and associate it specifically with Zuckerman.

topics.title: McClelland's Needs: Achievement, Affiliation and Power
topics.explanation: Compare the three social motives by the goals they orient behaviour toward.

topics.title: Motivational Competence
topics.explanation: Study this as the ability to mobilize and regulate motivation in relation to goals and behaviour, keeping the term within the syllabus context.

topics.title: Self-Regulation
topics.explanation: Study goal-directed monitoring and regulation of one's behaviour, cognition and motivation.

topics.title: Flow
topics.explanation: Study flow as a distinctive state of deep involvement/optimal experience associated with activity engagement.

topics.title: Physiological Correlates of Emotion
topics.explanation: Study bodily and physiological changes associated with emotional states.

topics.title: Theories of Emotion
topics.explanation: Make a comparison table of the five named theories, especially the role of physiological arousal and cognition.

topics.title: Emotion Regulation
topics.explanation: Study processes used to monitor, modify or manage emotional responses.

topics.title: Conflicts
topics.explanation: Study psychological conflict, its sources and major types as specified in the syllabus.

topics.title: Stress and Coping
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Stress and Coping, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

topics.title: Stress Management Strategies
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Stress Management Strategies, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

topics.title: Seligman's Explanatory Styles and Learned Helplessness

units.title: Social Psychology
units.description: Understand social behaviour by examining how people perceive others, form and change attitudes, influence one another, function in groups, and relate across social and intergroup boundaries. Connect individual-level processes such as social cognition and attitude formation with influence, group processes, interpersonal relationships, and intergroup relations. The goal is to build a coherent explanation of how social context shapes thought, feeling, and behaviour.

topics.title: Nature and History of Social Psychology
topics.explanation: Study what social psychology examines, its scope and major historical developments.

topics.title: Theoretical Perspectives in Social Psychology
topics.explanation: Compare the five perspectives by their explanation of social behaviour and the constructs they emphasize.

topics.title: Social Perception, Attitudes and Prosocial Behaviour
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Social Perception, Attitudes and Prosocial Behaviour, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

microtopics.title: Central and peripheral routes to persuasion
Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility

topics.title: Groups and Social Influence
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Groups and Social Influence, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

topics.title: Aggression
topics.explanation: Study aggression as social behaviour, including its forms, determinants and contextual influences.

topics.title: Group Dynamics and Leadership
topics.explanation: Study how groups function and how leadership styles relate to group effectiveness.

topics.title: Theories of Intergroup Relations
topics.explanation: Build a clear understanding of Theories of Intergroup Relations, then connect its key ideas, distinctions, and applications.

topics.title: Applied Social Psychology
topics.explanation: Connect social-psychological principles with health, environmental and legal contexts, and study personal space, crowding and territoriality.

units.title: Human Development and Interventions
units.description: Trace psychological development across the lifespan and use that developmental perspective to understand major areas of psychological intervention. Connect developmental changes with psychopathology, psychotherapy, education, guidance, and counselling, while keeping the person’s age, context, and needs in view. This unit helps you distinguish developmental concepts from intervention approaches and understand where each becomes relevant.

topics.title: Developmental Processes
topics.explanation: Study development through nature, principles, factors and stages. Keep biological and environmental influences conceptually distinct but interactive.

topics.title: Successful Aging
topics.explanation: Study successful aging as a developmental outcome and organize its psychological and contextual dimensions.

topics.title: Theories of Development
topics.explanation: Compare psychoanalytic, behavioristic and cognitive explanations of development.

topics.title: Domains of Development
topics.explanation: Create a domain map and track how each developmental domain changes across stages.

topics.title: Psychopathology
topics.explanation: Study the conceptualization of psychopathology, the components/purpose of mental status examination, classification and causal perspectives.

topics.title: Psychotherapies
topics.explanation: Build a therapy comparison matrix: theoretical orientation, target/problem, therapist role, client role, key techniques and distinctive terminology. Use the exact list in the syllabus as the checklist.

topics.title: Motivation and Learning in Schools
topics.explanation: Study how motivational and learning principles can be translated into educational practice.

microtopics.title: Applications of motivation theories in school
Applications of learning theories in school

topics.title: Educational Achievement
topics.explanation: Organize educational achievement factors into learner, instructional, environmental and contextual influences.

topics.title: Teacher Effectiveness
topics.explanation: Study teacher effectiveness as a psychological/educational construct and identify factors that influence effective teaching.

topics.title: Guidance in Schools
topics.explanation: Study why schools need guidance, how guidance can be organized institutionally, and the major techniques used.

topics.title: Counselling: Process, Skills and Techniques
topics.explanation: Study counselling as a helping process, emphasizing process stages, core skills and techniques.

microtopics.title: Basic counselling skills: listening, questioning and empathy

units.title: Emerging Areas
units.description: Explore areas in which psychology responds to changing social, cultural, health, environmental, and digital realities. Examine diversity and inequality alongside wellbeing, health, peace, and the psychological consequences of contemporary and digital life. Use the unit to connect established psychological principles with emerging problems and applications, while recognising how context changes the questions psychologists ask and the interventions they design.

topics.title: Gender, Poverty, Disability and Migration
topics.explanation: Study each issue through cultural bias, discrimination and the psychological/social consequences of marginalization.

topics.title: Stigma, Marginalisation, Abuse and Violence
topics.explanation: Connect stigma and marginalization with social suffering, then study child abuse and domestic violence as important applied concerns.

topics.title: Peace Psychology
topics.explanation: Study peace psychology through violence, non-violence, macro-level conflict resolution and media's role.

microtopics.title: Role of media in conflict resolution

topics.title: Wellbeing and Self-Growth
topics.explanation: Compare hedonic and eudemonic wellbeing, then connect wellbeing with character strengths, resilience and post-traumatic growth.

topics.title: Health and Health Behaviour
topics.explanation: Build a health-psychology map linking behaviours and lifestyle with chronic disease and psychoneuroimmunology.

topics.title: Psychology and Technology
topics.explanation: Study psychological issues at the technology interface: digital learning, etiquette, cyberbullying, cyber pornography and parental mediation.
